chapter_theme: Civakan and Suramanjari unite in secret in Kama's shrine; he swears to wed her next day, she discloses the union through friend, foster mother and mother to her father Kuberadattan, who gives her to Civakan before the fire with a great dowry.

cast.role: the hero, in disguise in Suramanjari's city, called வேலான் and காமதிலகன் here
the merchant's daughter who had vowed to shun men, now united with and wed to Civakan
Civakan's friends, who ask for Suramanjari in marriage
Suramanjari's maid and friend, to whom she discloses the union
Suramanjari's father, the merchant Kuberadattan (named in 2076)

2060.reading: Suramanjari stands before Civakan with her face a little turned, garland and hair hanging, one gem earring throwing light like a rainbow, melting with love.
2060.event: Suramanjari stands melting before Civakan in Kama's shrine.

2061.reading: Civakan says the line of fine hair rising from her jewelled navel, like a single ray shot upward from a sapphire, came and carried off his firm restraint.
2061.nuance: The restraint that is lost here is the man's own (என் திண்ணிறை), in the chapter whose heroine had vowed that no one would break hers.

2062.reading: Saying that he took her for a goddess, that he will not live unless he touches her, and that he came to worship her small feet and begs her grace, Civakan bows, faints with love and embraces her on the couch while Anangan shoots his arrows.
2062.nuance: தேறினேன் தெய்வம் என்றே may also mean that she trusted the god's answer of 2058, which was his friend's trick; either way the worship she offered Kama for him is now offered by him to her.
2062.event: Civakan worships Suramanjari as a goddess and embraces her.

2063.reading: The woman of the peacock's grace and the man of the hill-defeating chest, matchless both, enjoyed by the proper way the pleasure of the natural union of sweet Tamil so that it would last.
2063.nuance: இன்றமிழ் இயற்கை இன்பம் names the Tamil grammar of love: the first secret union (இயற்கைப் புணர்ச்சி) of the akam poems, and நெறியின் claims the union keeps that rule.
2063.event: Civakan and Suramanjari are united in secret.

2064.reading: Afterwards he strokes her saffron-painted breasts to cool them, sets right the beads of her girdle, brushes the pollen from her anklets, crowns her with a garland and arranges her hair.
2064.event: Civakan adorns Suramanjari again after their union.

2065.reading: Civakan tells her that Kama bent both his bows straight and gave them to her as brows, and gave her a pair of flesh-fed arrows dipped in cool blood as eyes, because he wanted him to live.
2065.nuance: The closing என்னை உளனாக வேண்டினானே is turned: the weapons that wound him are said to be given so that he may stay alive, which is the lover's paradox and may also mean that Kama wanted him to exist only as her captive.

2066.reading: When Civakan praises her, saying that sky and earth together are the price of her breasts and that the lord of the ancient great ones made her as an ornament for womankind, she is shy, looks down at the flowers and bends like a branch heavy with blossom.
2066.event: Civakan praises Suramanjari and she bows her head in shyness.

2067.reading: Taking the bowed girl on his thigh, Civakan swears that if he does not join her beauty tomorrow he may become a king whose guarding lets dharma leave, and bids her go.
2067.nuance: The oath is a self-curse, and the penalty he names is a king's failure, though he passes as a merchant's son: the hidden prince swears by the sceptre he has not yet regained. நாளை promises marriage, which 2078 keeps. The reading of அறந்தலை நீங்கக் காக்கும் as 'guarding so that dharma departs' is the plainest the words allow but is not certain.
2067.event: Civakan swears an oath to wed Suramanjari the next day and sends her away.

claims.claim: to be a king under whose guard dharma departs is the worst fate a man can call down on himself

2068.reading: She folds her ringed fingers in due form and bows at his feet; told not to tremble but to go, she sways away with anklets and girdle chiming and reaches her company.
2068.event: Suramanjari bows to Civakan, leaves him and rejoins her companions.

2069.reading: Leaving her sweetness with the jewelled man, the girl of the spear-like eyes mounts the gem palanquin and enters her golden mansion.
2069.event: Suramanjari returns home in her palanquin.

2070.reading: While Civakan, his garland dripping honey like a rainbow that learns to rain, sits as the peerless prince Kamatilakan, his friends go to speak of marriage for the girl of the bow-like brows.
2070.nuance: காமதிலகன் may be a name under which the friends present him, as he is in disguise in this ilampakam, or only an epithet; the verse does not settle it.
2070.event: Civakan's friends go to ask for Suramanjari in marriage.

2071.reading: They make their proposal concerning the girl, a flowering creeper painted with the sea's nectar and honey, whose waist can hardly bear her, wearing a garland where bees sing.
2071.event: Civakan's friends ask for Suramanjari in marriage.

2072.reading: Hearing that she is asked for the master, the merchant, like a man with hot honey in his mouth, can neither swallow nor spit, and grieves that he and his daughter alike have done no penance, while the girl turns the matter over in her own mind.
2072.nuance: The father who bought a royal order to keep men from her (907) is caught between the offer and her vow; he blames neither the suitor nor her but their lack of earlier penance (நோற்றிலாதேன் நோற்றிலாள்).
2072.event: Suramanjari's father hears the proposal and cannot decide, while she deliberates.

claims.claim: what befalls a man and his child follows the penance they did or did not do

2073.reading: Leaning on a coral pillar like lightning on a garlanded post, waving the garland of chastity and driving off the drunken bee of shame, she stands before her friend and tells her, with no flaw in her words, as dharma requires.
2073.nuance: அறத்தினோடு நின்றாள் is the akam convention அறத்தொடு நிற்றல், disclosing a secret union so that it may end in marriage; the image sets chastity above shame, since she must put shame away for chastity's sake.
2073.event: Suramanjari discloses her union with Civakan to her friend.

2074.reading: Knowing her chastity, the friend puts a garland on her, bows at her feet, blesses her and goes to tell the foster mother.
2074.event: Suramanjari's friend tells the foster mother.

2075.reading: The foster mother tells Sumati, the girl's mother, that this is the girl's heart, and the mother says she saw in a dream in the thick dark a lovely flower pond run dry, and that so today the girl's maidenhood has gone.
2075.nuance: Who speaks the dream is not marked: கண்டேன் ... என்றாள் follows the foster mother's report and is most naturally the mother's answer, but it may continue the foster mother's words.
2075.event: The foster mother tells Sumati, who recalls a dream that foretold the loss of the girl's maidenhood.

2076.reading: The wife tells Kuberadattan of great fame, father of the girl whose face is a moon with fish, bow, coral, pearls and earrings in it.
2076.event: Sumati tells Kuberadattan of their daughter's union.

2077.reading: She tells him that their small, too-wise daughter kept this chastity of hers against all, and that the very man who made her powder lose has won her: the honey rain of fortune has fallen into the sea of milk.
2077.nuance: The mother turns the girl's grievance into proof: the vow taken in anger at Civakan's verdict (904, 908) is read as chastity kept for Civakan. பெருவளைப் பிட்டுக் காத்த is obscure.

2078.reading: Glad of what he hears, the merchant tells all his kin, prepares food, cloth, jewels, garlands and sandal for everyone without lack, and with drums sounding gives his daughter to the man of the fresh garland.
2078.event: Kuberadattan gives Suramanjari to Civakan in marriage.

2079.reading: He says that before the fire he has given his daughter a hundred and eight women with anklets, skilled in dance and the vina, one and a half crore of red gold, and three villages.
2079.nuance: The bride is given before the fire (எரியழல் முன்னர்), and with her a dowry the father declares himself.
2079.event: Kuberadattan declares the dowry given with his daughter before the fire.

2080.reading: He with jewel-bright body and a chest like a garlanded hill, and she like a gem-hung branch, sink into a sea of pleasure mingled without flaw.
2080.event: Civakan and Suramanjari live in wedded pleasure.

links.note: Suramanjari vowed that no one but Civakan would break her restraint; now Civakan says her beauty has carried off his.
links.teaches: The vow that guarded her நிறை against all men is answered by the loss of his, so the restraint the story set out to test breaks first on the man's side.

links.note: She knelt in Kama's shrine and begged the god for Civakan's chest; he now bows to her feet as to a goddess and begs her grace.
links.teaches: Worship runs both ways in one shrine: the girl's prayer to Kama for the man is turned into the man's prayer to the girl, so the deity she addressed is replaced by the lovers themselves.

links.note: Civakan swore to join her tomorrow on pain of becoming a king who lets dharma go; her father gives her to him in marriage.
links.teaches: The oath sworn in secret is kept through the father's public gift, so the secret union is made lawful by the kin rather than by the lovers alone.

links.note: Kural 560 says that if the guardian does not guard, the cows' yield fails and the learned forget their books; Civakan's oath calls such a guardian's fate down on himself if he fails her.
links.teaches: The bent sceptre that the Kural treats as a public disaster becomes, in a lover's oath, the worst private penalty a man can name, which shows how deep the guardian's duty sat as a measure of shame.

gains.a: the oath gains its weight: without the couplet's picture of a land ruined by an unguarding king, the curse Civakan names would read as a stock phrase
gains.b: the couplet gains a use as an oath-penalty, showing that failing to guard was held a dishonour fit to stake a promise on, not only a policy failure

links.note: The father bought a king's order to keep men from his daughter; now that a suitor asks for her he can neither accept nor refuse.
links.teaches: His wealth could shut out a whole city's men but cannot settle a single proposal, and he falls back on the lack of past penance to explain a bind his money made.

links.note: Kural 270 says the destitute are many because few do penance; the rich merchant says he and his daughter have done none.
links.teaches: The couplet ties lack to the absence of penance; the epic puts the same reasoning in a rich man's mouth, so the want that penance would have prevented is a want of good fortune in a child, not of wealth.

gains.a: the merchant's cry gains a doctrine behind it, that misfortune is the fruit of austerity not done, which makes his helplessness a moral account rather than a complaint
gains.b: the couplet gains a case where the one who lacks is wealthy, showing that its இலர் need not mean the poor

links.note: Kural 1251 makes restraint a door bolted by shame, broken by desire's axe; Suramanjari drives off the bee of shame and waves the garland of chastity.
links.teaches: In the couplet restraint stands only while shame bars it; the epic has a woman put shame away in order to keep her chastity, so the two virtues the couplet binds together are parted and ranked.

gains.a: the epic image gains a known structure to depart from, so that her casting off shame reads as a choice for chastity rather than a fall
gains.b: the couplet gains a counter-case in which shame is given up without restraint failing, which shows its door-and-bolt bond is not the only order of the two

links.note: In Kuruntokai 333 the friend asks what harm there would be in revealing their secret; in the epic the girl discloses it to her friend, who carries it to the foster mother, then the mother, then the father.
links.teaches: The Sangam friend only proposes disclosure; the epic plays out the whole chain of telling through friend, foster mother and mother to the father, which ends in marriage the same day.

gains.a: the epic scene gains its name and purpose: it is the akam move of disclosing so that kin will arrange the marriage, not a confession
gains.b: the Sangam poem's single question gains the full sequence it sets going, showing who carries the secret and to whom

links.note: The mother dreamed that a flower pond ran dry and reads it as the girl's maidenhood gone; the secret union of 2063 is the event.
links.teaches: The dream is read after the event it pictures, so it serves the mother as confirmation of what the foster mother reported rather than as a warning.

links.note: The mother once told the father that their daughter burned with anger at Civakan's verdict on her powder; now she tells him the same man has won her.
links.teaches: The grievance that made the girl shun all men is reread as the cause of her chastity for one man, so the anger and the love are shown to have had one object.

links.note: Akananuru 86 recalls a wedding of rice, sand, lamps, water poured with petals and paddy by four mothers, and the kin giving the bride; the epic father gives his daughter before the fire with a dowry he announces.
links.teaches: Set beside the Sangam wedding, which names no fire and no dowry, the epic's gift before the flame with women, gold and villages shows the giving of a bride recast as a fire rite with property declared.

gains.a: the epic verse gains a measure of what is new in it, the fire and the declared dowry, against an older Tamil wedding
gains.b: the Sangam poem gains a later counterpart that shows by contrast what its rite lacks: a sacred fire and a stated transfer of wealth

source_issues: 2060-2062, 2064-2067, 2070, 2072, 2073, 2075-2077 and 2079 were printed in eight half-lines and joined into four (FLAG repaired); the joins read correctly.
2065 and 2066 are in a longer metre than the verses around them (lines of seven to eight feet).
The print gives ோ where the sense needs ேர்: சோந்து (2062, for சோர்ந்து), சோத்தி (2074, for சேர்த்தி), நோந்தேன் (2079, for நேர்ந்தேன்).
2077 line 2 பெருவளைப் பிட்டுக் காத்த is obscure.
2079 line 3-4 (கோடி மூன்று ரெரியழன்) is divided across the line break; read as கோடி, மூன்று ஊர், எரியழல்.
2070 line 3 காமதிலகன் may be a name or an epithet.
